Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.
Mr. A.N. Sharma, Advocate, for the 
petitioner. 
Mr. Bhuwan Bhatt, Advocate, for the 
respondents. 
In both writ petitions, petitioner has 
moved application for impleadment of 
Cantonment Board, Bareilly.
Vide judgment and order dated 
8.3.2007 (impugned in WPMS/213/2007),
passed by the appellate authority under 
Section 22 of U.P. Urban Buildings 
(Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) 
Act, 1972, learned District Judge has 
allowed the release application filed by the 
landlord. It is not in dispute that petitioner 
had admitted respondent to be his landlord. 
In the impleadment applications, he 
contends that since the property belongs to 
the Cantonment Board, therefore, 
respondent is not the owner of the property. 
Hence, respondent ought not to have filed 
application for release of the building. 
In the humble opinion of this Court, 
impleadment applications have to be 
rejected as the issue raised in these 
applications cannot be decided in 
proceedings under U.P. Act No. 13 of 1972. 
While deciding release application, the 
Prescribed Authority has to see as to 
whether any relationship of landlord and 
tenant exists between the parties. Such 
relationship was admitted by the petitioner  in his written statement. Thus, now, he 
cannot turn around and question the status 
of the respondent. 
Accordingly, impleadment 
applications (IA/9577/2021 and 
IA/3431/2021) are rejected. 
List on 20.10.2022 after fresh 
matters.
 (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.)
 22.8.2022
Pr

of four days in filing restoration 
application. Learned counsel for 
applicant submits that the order, 
restoration whereof has been sought,
was passed on 09.08.2023; applicant 
applied for certified copy of the said
order on 11.08.2023; certified copy was 
prepared on 16.08.2023 which was 
delivered on 22.08.2023 and restoration 
application was filed on 12.09.2023. 
Thus, he submits that six days period 
spent in preparing certified copy of the 
order has to be excluded while 
computing the period of limitation. He 
further submits that restoration 
application was filed on 34th day from 
which six days time spent in preparing 
certified copy has to be excluded, thus it 
is to be deemed that the application was 
filed within time. He further submits 
that limitation for filing restoration 
application is 30 days, therefore, 
restoration application was filed in time.
(4) This Court find substance in the 
contention made by learned counsel for 
the applicant and the objection raised by  Registry is overruled. 
(5) For the reason indicated in the 
restoration applications, the same (MCC 
No. 9579 of 2023 and MCC No. 3433 of 
2023) are allowed. 
(6) The petitions are restored to their
original numbers, along with interim 
order(s), if any.
(7) List this case on 28.12.2023.
